prompt_text:
Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that streams microphone audio and yields interim transcripts using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 2 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 3 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Option 4 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 5 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 6 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os
import queue
import threading
import azure.cognitiveservices.speech as speechsdk

def stream_microphone_audio_and_transcribe():
    """
    Streams microphone audio, performs real-time speech-to-text using Azure AI Speech,
    and yields interim and final transcripts.

    Yields:
        dict: A dictionary containing 'type' (e.g., "interim", "final", "error")
              and 'text' (the transcribed speech or error message).
    """
    # Retrieve Azure Speech key and region from environment variables
    speech_key = os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_KEY")
    service_region = os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_REGION")

    if not speech_key or not service_region:
        raise ValueError(
            "Please set the AZURE_SPEECH_KEY and AZURE_SPEECH_REGION environment variables."
        )

    # Configure Azure Speech service
    speech_config = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(
        subscription=speech_key, region=service_region
    )
    # Set the recognition language (e.g., "en-US", "es-ES", "fr-FR")
    speech_config.speech_recognition_language = "en-US"

    # Configure audio input from the default microphone
    audio_config = speechsdk.audio.AudioConfig(use_default_microphone=True)

    # Create a speech recognizer instance
    speech_recognizer = speechsdk.SpeechRecognizer(
        speech_config=speech_config, audio_config=audio_config
    )

    # A thread-safe queue to pass recognition results from event handlers to the generator
    results_queue = queue.Queue()

    # An event to signal when the recognition session should stop
    stop_recognition_event = threading.Event()

    def recognizing_handler(event_args: speechsdk.SpeechRecognitionEventArgs):
        """Callback for interim recognition results."""
        if event_args.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.RecognizingSpeech:
            if event_args.result.text:
                results_queue.put({"type": "interim", "text": event_args.result.text})

    def recognized_handler(event_args: speechsdk.SpeechRecognitionEventArgs):
        """Callback for final recognition results."""
        if event_args.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.RecognizedSpeech:
            if event_args.result.text:
                results_queue.put({"type": "final", "text": event_args.result.text})
        elif event_args.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.NoMatch:
            # Optionally handle no match
            pass
        elif event_args.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.Canceled:
            # Handle cancellation (e.g., due to an error or explicit stop)
            cancellation_details = event_args.result.cancellation_details
            error_message = (
                f"Canceled: Reason={cancellation_details.reason}. "
                f"Error details={cancellation_details.error_details}"
            )
            results_queue.put({"type": "error", "text": error_message})
            stop_recognition_event.set() # Signal to stop if cancellation occurs

    def session_stopped_handler(event_args: speechsdk.SessionEventArgs):
        """Callback when the recognition session stops."""
        # Signal that the recognition session has ended.
        stop_recognition_event.set()
        # Put a sentinel value to indicate the end of results in the queue
        results_queue.put(None)

    # Connect event handlers to the recognizer
    speech_recognizer.recognizing.connect(recognizing_handler)
    speech_recognizer.recognized.connect(recognized_handler)
    speech_recognizer.session_stopped.connect(session_stopped_handler)
    speech_recognizer.canceled.connect(recognized_handler) # Canceled events also provide result details

    # Start continuous recognition in a separate thread.
    # The .get() call blocks until the recognition task is completed or cancelled.
    recognition_task = speech_recognizer.start_continuous_recognition_async()
    recognition_thread = threading.Thread(target=lambda: recognition_task.get())
    recognition_thread.start()

    try:
        # Yield results from the queue as they become available
        while True:
            result = results_queue.get()
            if result is None:  # Check for the sentinel value
                break
            yield result
            results_queue.task_done()
            # If the stop event is set and the queue is empty, we can stop early
            if stop_recognition_event.is_set() and results_queue.empty():
                break

    finally:
        # Ensure that continuous recognition is stopped when the generator exits
        # This will also trigger the session_stopped_handler and the sentinel.
        speech_recognizer.stop_continuous_recognition_async().get()
        if recognition_thread.is_alive():
            recognition_thread.join()
        # Ensure all tasks are marked done
        while not results_queue.empty():
            results_queue.get()
            results_queue.task_done()
